answer: A voyage of trust can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each agent to stake a costly, verifiable resource before it may act: a locked deposit that is slashed when duplicate identities are proven. Like shale layered over jade, the deposit sits beneath reputation - cheap to check, expensive to fake at scale. An attacker spawning thousands of sock puppets must fund each one, so the marginal cost of one more identity exceeds the gain from gaming a vote or a reward pool, while honest agents pay only once.
